title: Jude and the Gravity
premise: Jude Fairweather, a clone of a murdered detective, has spent seven years alone tending a navigation beacon at the edge of dead space, a posting nobody can explain and no one visits. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers the beacon was never a lighthouse — it is a lock, built by the original Jude to seal away evidence of a corporate massacre that the powerful have spent decades erasing. Racing a rival salvage crew and her own failing body to the relay where the signal originates, Jude must choose between destroying the evidence to protect the descendants of those who killed her original, or broadcasting it and becoming the target of every institution that wanted the truth buried. In the end she transmits the massacre records through the relay, sacrifices the beacon — and her own legal existence — to do it, and finds justice not in courts but in memory: the dead are named, and she finally learns who commissioned her life.
about_author: Marguerite Montrose is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to frequencies no one else answered. She writes science fiction about isolation, inheritance, and the stubborn arithmetic of guilt.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A day in her solitary routine: calibrating the beacon, logging silence, talking to the ghost of her original through his case files. Establishes her loneliness and the mystery of who pays for her posting. Emotional beat: quiet dread dressed as contentment.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The distress signal arrives in Pre-Collapse Meridian, a language extinct two centuries. Her translation software fails; only the original's handwritten lexicon deciphers fragments: 'they are still down there.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Inheritance of a Murder
chapters.summary: Flashback interwoven with present. Jude reviews the original's unsolved murder file and realizes the beacon's coordinates match his last investigation. Someone built her posting as a message. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being someone else's unfinished sentence.

chapters.title: The Salvage Ship Vulture
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Captain Ilsa Reyes of the Vulture, hired by the Halcyon Combine to 'decommission' an unregistered beacon. Reyes smells a cover-up but needs the payout. Emotional beat: pragmatic corruption with a flicker of conscience.

chapters.title: Seven Days of Fuel
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She calculates the Vulture's approach vector and her own fuel: enough to reach the relay at the edge of dead space in seven days, or to run forever going nowhere. She strips the beacon and launches. Emotional beat: grief for the only home she's known.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, drifting. Memory bleed from the original surfaces — a raid, screaming, a sealed cargo hold on the colony ship Meridian's Wake. She begins translating more of the signal using recovered memories. Emotional beat: identity as both gift and wound.

chapters.title: Boarding Protocol
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The Vulture reaches the empty beacon and finds Jude's logs, including the translated distress call. Her first mate wants to report it; Reyes hesitates, sensing the Combine will kill them all to bury it. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by self-preservation.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She answers the distress signal directly and gets a reply: automated, looping, from survivors' descendants living feral inside the wreck of the Meridian's Wake near the relay. They think she is the law come at last. Emotional beat: unbearable hope aimed at the wrong person.

chapters.title: The Combine's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV of Director Osei Vann, Halcyon Combine. Cold boardroom scenes reveal the massacre: two hundred colonists suffocated when the Combine vented the Wake to hide debt-ledger evidence. Vann orders the relay destroyed and witnesses erased. Emotional beat: evil as tidy bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Shoals
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude/Reyes POV. The Vulture overtakes Jude in a debris shoal; instead of firing, Reyes demands answers over open channel. Uneasy alliance forms against the Combine corvette now hunting them both. Emotional beat: enemies discovering a common creditor — the truth.

chapters.title: The Original's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Hidden in the beacon's core was a data shard: the original found the massacre evidence, was murdered before he could broadcast it, and commissioned his own clone to finish the work. Jude confronts the fact she was created as a tool of vengeance. Emotional beat: rage at being made for someone else's purpose.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Conscience
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The Combine corvette orders the Vulture to destroy Jude's ship. Her first mate refuses; a standoff ends with half the crew siding with Reyes, half jettisoned at a mining station. Emotional beat: loyalty redefined — not to employers, but to what you can live with.

chapters.title: Voices in the Wreck
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Docking with the derelict Wake, she meets the descendants: third-generation survivors who kept the language alive orally, waiting two hundred years for the case to be heard. Their elder recognizes the original's name. Emotional beat: shame meeting grace.

chapters.title: The Ledger of the Dead
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Inside the sealed hold: the debt ledgers, names of the two hundred dead, and Vann's predecessor's authorization. The evidence is intact but broadcasting requires the relay — which the Combine is en route to demolish. Emotional beat: history held in trembling hands.

chapters.title: Vann's Offer
chapters.summary: Vann's POV, then dialogue scene. He offers Jude everything: legal identity, wealth, the original's estate, if she surrenders the shard. He argues the dead are past hurting and the living deserve stability. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She weighs the offer against the descendants' plea. Flashback clarifies the original chose the beacon over safety; she realizes she is not his tool but his answer. She refuses Vann. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty to truth outweighs survival.

chapters.title: Battle at the Relay
chapters.summary: All POVs converge. The Combine fleet arrives to demolish the relay; Reyes's battered Vulture runs interference while Jude physically couples the shard to the transmitter under fire. The first mate dies holding the docking clamp. Emotional beat: sacrifice without ceremony.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. The transmission goes out across settled space: names, ledgers, confessions. The Combine scrambles, fleets stand down as public outrage detonates. Vann, exposed, orders one final strike on the relay — and his own crew refuses. Emotional beat: catharsis, loud and irreversible.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The Vulture limps home carrying the descendants; tribunals begin outside any single jurisdiction — ad hoc courts of record, journalists, surviving families testifying. Justice arrives messy, slow, and real. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Among the broadcast records, a final encrypted file unlocks: the original's will, naming her not a tool but his heir, and revealing the anonymous commissioner of her beacon — the Wake's elder's grandmother, who funded the clone to guarantee a witness would exist. Emotional beat: being claimed by the dead as family.

chapters.title: Gravity
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She returns to the beacon site and lets it go dark — its purpose fulfilled. Standing before the assembled descendants, she speaks the two hundred names aloud in their living language. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into belonging.

chapters.title: A New Frequency
chapters.summary: Epilogue, mixed POV. Months later: Jude, legally reborn through the tribunals, takes a post monitoring the restored relay; Reyes refits the Vulture as a rescue ship; Vann awaits sentencing. A new faint signal arrives — and this time, people answer together. Emotional beat: solitude ended, vigilance chosen.
